documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

55 y/o woman transferring care; prior PCP retiring. Brought her bottles.

Hx:
- HTN for ~10 yrs. Amlodipine 10 + HCTZ 25. Doesn't check at home.
- T2DM dx about 8 yrs ago. Metformin 1000 bid, glargine 20 u qhs. Says sugars "have never been great"; recent outside A1c values in the low 8s per her report. Checks fingersticks a few times a week, fasting mostly.
- RA since her late 30s, seropositive. Outside rheumatologist, seen about yearly. MTX 15 mg weekly + folic acid, prednisone 5 daily for about 10 yrs. Hands are "okay most days."
- Iron deficiency anemia, on ferrous sulfate. Colonoscopy at 50 had a polyp removed; she has not been back.
- Bone density "a little thin" on a scan at the old office, put down to the steroid.

PSH: C-section at 28. Colonoscopy w/ polypectomy at 50.
FH: Mother - T2DM, HTN, stroke at 72. Father - CAD, MI at 68. Sister - seropositive RA. Maternal aunt - breast cancer (IDC) at 62.
SH: Part-time bookkeeper. Smokes ~1 ppd, 30 pack-years. Wine a glass or two a month. No drugs.
Allergies: NKDA.

ROS: negative except as above. No chest pain, dyspnea, edema, GI bleeding, melena.

Exam: Pleasant, in no distress. Vitals per flowsheet. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, low transverse scar. Ext: no edema. Hands: mild MCP thickening bilaterally, no warmth or effusion. Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+, monofilament intact both feet.

A/P:
1. T2DM, not at goal by history. A1c, CMP, UACR today. Continue metformin and glargine for now; revisit once I have numbers.
2. HTN - reasonable today. Continue amlodipine/HCTZ.
3. RA on MTX/pred - per rheumatology. CBC and LFTs here every few months if she wants them local; she does.
4. IDA - CBC, iron studies. Overdue surveillance colonoscopy given prior adenoma and the anemia: GI referral.
5. Steroid osteopenia - will get the old DXA from her records; repeat when due.
6. Tobacco - 30 pk-yr, current. Talked about quitting; she isn't ready. Qualifies for annual LDCT - ordered.
7. HM: Tdap today. HCV and HIV screening today. Screening mammogram ordered (last one last fall, normal per pt).

Records release on file. RTC 3 months.

OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - PROCEDURE REPORT

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 03/09/2022
Reason: leg swelling.

Thank you for referring Ms. Krause, 58, about three months after her last diabetes visit with you. For two months both legs have been getting progressively puffier, worst toward evening and a bit better after a night with her feet up. She has had no chest pain, no breathlessness and no long trips.

History: hypertension, type 2 diabetes (poorly controlled), rheumatoid arthritis, iron deficiency anemia, osteopenia from long-term steroids. Medications: amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metformin, insulin glargine, methotrexate, prednisone, ferrous sulfate, folic acid. Allergies: NKDA. Family: father with CAD and MI at 68; mother diabetes, hypertension, stroke at 72. Smokes one pack daily, 30 pack-years.

Exam: BP 142/88, HR 78, RR 16. 2+ pitting edema to the mid-shin on both sides. Remainder of the cardiovascular and general exam unremarkable.

Labs today: sodium 140, potassium 4.2, creatinine 1.0, BUN 14, albumin 4.5. Urinalysis without protein or blood.

Impression: Dependent bilateral edema from the calcium channel blocker. Normal renal function and albumin with no proteinuria argue against a renal or hepatic cause, and there are no features of heart failure.

Recommendations: Elevate the legs when seated. The amlodipine is the likely cause; whether to lower or replace it I will leave to you, as her pressure is above goal today. No cardiology follow-up needed unless new symptoms.

documents.title: Breast Surgery Consultation
documents.author: breast surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE BREAST SURGERY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 12/05/2022

Ms. Krause is a 58-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes that has been hard to control and rheumatoid arthritis on long-term prednisone. For half a year she has had an itchy scaly eruption on the right nipple and areola. It started as a small red flaky spot, has gradually spread, and now and then oozes clear fluid. No nipple discharge and she has felt no lump.

Medications: amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, metformin, insulin glargine, methotrexate, prednisone 5 mg, ferrous sulfate, folic acid. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: maternal aunt with invasive ductal breast cancer at 62.
Social: 30 pack-years, still smoking.

Exam: Right nipple-areolar complex erythematous with excoriations and a small area of ulceration. No mass in either breast. No palpable axillary adenopathy.

Imaging: diagnostic mammogram today shows a subtle area of increased density on the right without a discrete mass or calcifications.

Procedure: 4 mm punch biopsy of the right nipple skin under local anesthesia, tolerated well.

Impression: Unilateral nipple dermatitis concerning for Paget disease. Will call her with pathology and plan.

reports.text: Specimen: skin, right nipple, punch biopsy. Epidermis infiltrated by single and clustered large cells with abundant pale cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli. Immunostains: tumor cells CK7 positive.
reports.conclusion: Paget disease of the nipple.

documents.author: PCP

PRE-OPERATIVE EVALUATION
Planned: right breast surgery (central lumpectomy) in January for biopsy-proven Paget disease of the nipple.

Labs: hemoglobin 10.2, WBC 7.0, platelets 250.
Procedure: cervical biopsy of the lesion; hemostasis with silver nitrate.

Impression: Gross cervical lesion highly suspicious for carcinoma. Pathology pending; will refer on to gynecologic oncology if confirmed.

reports.text: Specimen: cervix, anterior lip, biopsy. Sheets and nests of atypical squamous cells with keratinization infiltrating the stroma.

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEPHROLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 11/29/2024

Thank you for sending Ms. Krause. She describes half a year of gradually worsening tiredness, a bloated abdomen and swelling of both legs. Background includes seropositive rheumatoid arthritis for over 20 years, treated with methotrexate and low-dose prednisone for roughly 15 of them, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, amlodipine-related ankle edema, iron deficiency anemia, Paget disease of the right nipple (2023) and stage IB2 cervical cancer (2024), both treated.

Medications: amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metformin 1000 mg bid, insulin glargine 20 units, ferrous sulfate, folic acid (plus methotrexate and prednisone as above). NKDA.

Exam: BP 140/90. 2+ pitting edema to the knees.

Results: albumin 2.8 g/dL; creatinine 1.2 mg/dL; 24-hour urine protein 4.5 g; urine microscopy bland, no cells or casts; CRP 25 mg/L. Serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation: no monoclonal protein.
Echocardiogram: normal LV function, no valve disease.
Abdominal fat pad biopsy: amorphous hyaline deposits, Congo red positive with apple-green birefringence; immunohistochemistry positive for serum amyloid A.

Impression: AA (secondary) amyloidosis from long-standing rheumatoid arthritis, with nephrotic-range proteinuria. No cardiac involvement on echo. No monoclonal protein to suggest AL.

Plan:
1. Losartan 25 mg daily started for proteinuria; BMP in 2 weeks - please draw at your office.
2. The key treatment is suppressing the inflammation driving amyloid production. I have written to her rheumatologist recommending escalation of RA therapy; an IL-6 receptor blocker is the usual choice.
3. Low-salt diet. Will see her again in 3 months.

OUTSIDE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN NOTE
Visit 05/29/2025

61F with RA (methotrexate, prednisone, tocilizumab per patient), type 2 diabetes, recently diagnosed AA amyloidosis. For about two weeks, sudden bouts of severe spinning whenever she rolls onto her right side in bed or tips her head back to reach a high cupboard. Each lasts under a minute and leaves her nauseated. No hearing change, no ringing, no weakness, numbness, speech or vision trouble. NKDA.

BP 130/85. Cardiovascular exam normal. Neurologic exam nonfocal: cranial nerves intact, normal finger-nose, normal gait.
Dix-Hallpike to the right: brief burst of nystagmus with vertigo lasting less than a minute, fading on its own.

Impression: benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, right.
Treatment: canalith repositioning (Epley) performed in the department; symptoms improved on re-testing.

OUTSIDE OPHTHALMOLOGY - ED CONSULTATION 12/03/2025 AND OPERATIVE SUMMARY 12/04/2025
(Records received on request; the ED record itself was not included.)

Consult: 61-year-old woman, called from the ED for painless loss of vision in the right eye starting three hours earlier, after she struck her head on a door frame. No flashes or floaters beforehand. History of diabetes, RA on immunosuppression, AA amyloidosis.
Visual acuity: OD 20/250, OS 20/25. Intraocular pressure normal both eyes. No pain, injection or photophobia. Left eye normal.
Dilated fundus exam OD: macula-off rhegmatogenous retinal detachment with a single retinal tear. OS: attached, no breaks.
Plan: urgent repair.

Operation 12/04/2025: pars plana vitrectomy, right eye, with endolaser to the break and gas tamponade. Uncomplicated.
Post-op: face-down positioning as instructed; no air travel or high altitude until the gas resolves. Drops per sheet. Follow-up with retina at 1 day, 1 week, then as directed. NKDA.

Visit 02/10/2026. Two months after vitrectomy with gas for a macula-off rhegmatogenous detachment of the right eye. Gas resolved. Retina attached 360 degrees. Visual acuity OD 20/80, OS 20/25. IOP normal. Plan: return in 3 months; report any new flashes, floaters or shadow promptly.

reports.text: Sigmoid colon wall thickening with pericolic fat stranding and a few small foci of extraluminal gas confined to the pericolic fat adjacent to the sigmoid. No drainable abscess. No free intraperitoneal air. No free fluid. Background sigmoid diverticulosis. Post-hysterectomy pelvis. Kidneys without hydronephrosis.
reports.conclusion: Acute sigmoid diverticulitis with localized perforation. No abscess.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY, GENERAL SURGERY
Admitted 06/04/2026. Discharged 06/13/2026.

62-year-old woman on immunosuppression for rheumatoid arthritis (methotrexate, prednisone 5 mg, tocilizumab), with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes, AA amyloidosis, treated cervical squamous cell carcinoma and Paget disease of the nipple, and a right retinal detachment repaired six months ago. Admitted with increasing abdominal pain and fever, T 38.3 on arrival.

CT: sigmoid diverticulitis with localized perforation (small extraluminal gas foci confined to the pericolic fat), no abscess.
Treatment: bowel rest, IV piperacillin-tazobactam. Methotrexate and tocilizumab held. Stress-dose hydrocortisone, later back to prednisone 5 mg. Glargine continued with correction insulin.

Over the first 48 hours she developed hematochezia with hemoglobin falling from 10.2 to 7.4 g/dL and received three units of packed red cells. Bleeding stopped without endoscopic or surgical intervention.

Several hours after the third unit (06/06 evening) she became acutely short of breath: RR 28, SpO2 84% on room air, HR 96, BP 118/72. She was in distress, using accessory muscles, with diffuse crackles at both bases and fields, no wheeze. Heart sounds normal; no JVD; no leg edema. Urine output unchanged. Portable chest film: bilateral infiltrates with a normal cardiac silhouette. NT-proBNP 180 pg/mL.
Diagnosis: transfusion-related acute lung injury. Transferred to ICU on high-flow nasal oxygen; not intubated. Improved over 72 hours; on room air from 06/10. Chest film 06/11 nearly clear. Blood bank notified and reaction reported to the supplier.

Hemoglobin 9.6 after transfusion, 9.3 at discharge.

Discharge diagnoses: complicated sigmoid diverticulitis with localized perforation; lower GI bleeding with acute blood loss anemia; transfusion-related acute lung injury.
Discharge medications: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily to complete 14 days of antibiotic therapy; resume home medications; HOLD tocilizumab until surgical follow-up.
Follow-up: general surgery clinic in 4 weeks; colonoscopy 6-8 weeks after recovery; PCP within 2 weeks.
Note for future care: any transfusion only after blood bank review given TRALI.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Patient Portal Message
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Patient: I was in the hospital June 4 to 13. Diverticulitis with a small hole in the bowel, then bleeding, then they gave me blood and my lungs filled up and I was in the ICU a few days. I'm home on antibiotics. They said see you in 2 weeks. I'm wiped out.

documents.title: Patient Portal Message
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Janet, I'm so sorry - that's a lot. Glad you're home. We don't have the hospital paperwork yet; I've asked for it. Please finish every antibiotic dose, go to the ER for fever, worsening belly pain, blood in the stool or any trouble breathing. Front desk will call to set up a visit.

documents.title: Scheduling Call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called to schedule hospital follow-up. Pt says her sister is driving her to the surgeon and eye appointments and she can't manage another trip this month; she'll call back when she has a ride. Offered video visit; she prefers in person.

documents.title: General Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GENERAL SURGERY - CLINIC FOLLOW-UP
Visit 07/14/2026. Follow-up after admission for perforated sigmoid diverticulitis complicated by lower GI bleeding and TRALI. Antibiotics completed. No abdominal pain, eating normally, no further bleeding. Breathing back to baseline. Abdomen soft, nontender.
Plan: colonoscopy with GI, booked for September 2026. Tocilizumab may be restarted per rheumatology. We will discuss elective sigmoid resection after the colonoscopy. NKDA.
